gb.description: Agreement: I Agree Body: Dear Editor The issue of who should be tested for H. pylori was addressed by Public Health England in a publication which stated that "patients with unexplained iron deficiency anaemia, after negative endoscopic investigation has excluded gastric and colonic malignancy, and investigations have been carried out for other causes, including cancer, idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura, vitamin B12 deficiency" should come under the heading of patients who should be tested for H. pylori[1]. In principle, those recommendations should apply even when a patient presents with unusual manifestations of iron deficiency anaemia such as koilonychia[2], or Plummer-Vinson syndrome[3],[4],5],[6]. Hence the rationale for H. pylori testing in a patient with Plummer-Vinson syndrome in whom duodenal biopsy was non diagnostic for coeliac disease, and in whom colonoscopy had also been non diagnostic for colon cancer [7]. H. pylori gastritis is also a risk factor for vitamin B12 deficiency[8] and, hence, subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord[9]. Accordingly, the workup of patients with vitamin B12 deficiency, including patients with myeloneuropathy attributable to nitrous oxide abuse[10] should include tests for H. pylori[10]. es.title: Desprecio al Parlamento
es.description: La iniciativa del Gobierno para convalidar en la Diputación Permanente del Congreso los decretos sobre vivienda que fueron rechazados en el Pleno tiene un encaje perfectamente legal. No es ese el problema. Pero desde el punto de vista político es un dislate, el último por ahora en una legislatura plagada de ellos, porque violenta la voluntad del órgano que constituye la representación de la soberanía nacional. Lo que hace Pedro Sánchez es utilizar un subterfugio reglamentario para convertir esos decretos en la avanzadilla de una campaña electoral para la que ya se ha dibujado un panorama de máxima tensión. El propio presidente, en algunas de las declaraciones públicas que ha hecho desde que lanzó la convocatoria de elecciones, ha justificado su decisión con la sorprendente afirmación de que el Congreso había dado la espalda a la ciudadanía. Que el jefe del Gobierno de una democracia ignore, o dé a entender que lo ignora, que el Pleno del Congreso no puede darle la espalda a la ciudadanía porque es su representación política más genuina da idea de hasta qué punto estamos en una deriva institucional alarmante. Pero esta anómala circunstancia solo es posible porque la correlación de mayorías y minorías de la Diputación Permanente es diferente de la del Pleno, una disfunción que no se entiende cuando el órgano que se encarga de los periodos de interinidad tiene competencias, como se ve en este caso, muy amplias. No se trata, por tanto, de valorar el contenido de los decretos de vivienda, sino de subrayar que por parte del Gobierno se desprecia una vez más al Parlamento, haciendo buena la declaración de Sánchez, realizada cuando Junts empezaba a desmarcarse de la coalición de intereses que propició la investidura, de que estaba dispuesto a gobernar al margen del Legislativo. En esta ocasión, además, lo manipula de una forma innoble y lo utiliza como elemento de su campaña electoral. Constituye una maniobra política que, como tantas otras actuaciones, tiene nulos precedentes en nuestro sistema democrático.

mx.title: Volkswagen también utiliza una correa de distribución bañada en aceite como la que dio problemas a otra marca, pero existe una diferencia crucial
mx.description: En años recientes los motores PureTech de Stellantis ganaron una enorme popularidad mundial, pero no precisamente por algo bueno. En realidad se hicieron famosos por la correa de distribución bañada en aceite, que se convirtió en un auténtico dolor de cabeza para la marca. Sin embargo, Volkswagen también ha utilizado una correa que trabaja sumergida en aceite, pero no se ha convertido en un problema gracias a una diferencia fundamental. La marca alemana incorporó este mecanismo en determinados motores diésel de la familia EA288, incluido el 2.0 TDI que llegó a modelos como el Volkswagen Golf de séptima generación. A primera vista, la solución parece similar a la de los motores PureTech, ya que es una correa dentada que trabaja en contacto directo con el lubricante del motor. En los motores 1.0 y 1.2L PureTech se comenzaba a degradar el material de la correa debido al contacto continuo con el aceite, por lo que algunos residuos se acumulaban y obstruían el sistema de lubricación, provocando problemas que podían ser catastróficos, ya que esta pieza formaba parte del sistema de distribución sincronizando el movimiento del cigüeñal con el árbol de levas. En cambio, los ingenieros de Volkswagen emplearon una correa bañada en aceite, pero no acciona la distribución. El trabajo de esta pieza consiste en transmitir el movimiento del cigüeñal a la bomba de aceite y a la bomba de vacío, mientras que la sincronización de las válvulas recae en una correa independiente, la cual no trabaja con el aceite del motor. Esta diferencia es crucial para la fiabilidad de los motores EA288, porque las correas cumplen funciones distintas. Aunque la banda húmeda de Volkswagen también puede sufrir desgaste y no está exenta de fallas, su arquitectura no reproduce las condiciones de los PureTech, donde la degradación de la correa de distribución compromete otros sistemas del motor. La idea detrás de una correa bañada en aceite es buena, ya que el objetivo es reducir la fricción y el ruido, pero la implementación no siempre es la mejor. En el caso de Stellantis, el material no es durable con el aceite y además se requiere de un mantenimiento exhaustivo o de lo contrario el motor puede morir prematuramente. Volkswagen logró esquivar la bala del problema más grande con sólo cambiar el uso que se le da a la banda, pero no necesariamente se eliminan por completo los riesgos de una correa bañada en aceite. - La noticia Volkswagen también utiliza una correa de distribución bañada en aceite como la que dio problemas a otra marca, pero existe una diferencia crucial fue publicada originalmente en Motorpasión México por Alonso Brugada .

in.title: Re: Clinical update: Assessment and management of Helicobacter pylori infection and who should be tested
in.description: Agreement: I Agree Body: Dear Editor The issue of who should be tested for H. pylori was addressed by Public Health England in a publication which stated that "patients with unexplained iron deficiency anaemia, after negative endoscopic investigation has excluded gastric and colonic malignancy, and investigations have been carried out for other causes, including cancer, idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura, vitamin B12 deficiency" should come under the heading of patients who should be tested for H. pylori[1]. In principle, those recommendations should apply even when a patient presents with unusual manifestations of iron deficiency anaemia such as koilonychia[2], or Plummer-Vinson syndrome[3],[4],5],[6]. Hence the rationale for H. pylori testing in a patient with Plummer-Vinson syndrome in whom duodenal biopsy was non diagnostic for coeliac disease, and in whom colonoscopy had also been non diagnostic for colon cancer [7]. H. pylori gastritis is also a risk factor for vitamin B12 deficiency[8] and, hence, subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord[9]. Accordingly, the workup of patients with vitamin B12 deficiency, including patients with myeloneuropathy attributable to nitrous oxide abuse[10] should include tests for H. pylori[10]. In the latter context eradication of H. pylori should be an adjunct to vitamin B12 replacement therapy[10]. References [1] McNulty C. Test and Treat for Helicobacter pylori(HP) in dyspepsia. in.title: J&V Energy Accelerates Low-Carbon Growth with Integrated Energy and Infrastructure Solutions
in.description: TAIPEI, Oct. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- J&V Energy Technology Co., Ltd. was recognized with the Corporate Excellence Award at the Asia Pacific Enterprise Awards (APEA) 2026 Taiwan Chapter, organized by Enterprise Asia, honoring its sustained growth and expanding contribution to the low-carbon energy transition. Established in 2016 and headquartered in Taipei, the company has evolved from a solar energy developer into a diversified energy and infrastructure group spanning renewable energy, green electricity trading, battery energy storage, water treatment, circular economy solutions, and AI infrastructure. J&V Energy's growth has been driven by its ability to combine technology, capital, and strategic partnerships across the energy value chain. The Group developed Taiwan's largest fishery-solar project at 128 MW, established Greenet as Taiwan's leading private green electricity trading platform, and developed Recharge Power into one of Taiwan's largest energy storage integrators. Recharge Power's cumulative deployments have reached 412 MW/1,055 MWh, including experience delivering Taiwan's largest single energy storage project. The Group's expanding operations now extend across Taiwan region, Japan, Australia, the Philippines, and other Asian markets. In 2025, the Group achieved 96.9% year-on-year growth in consolidated revenue and expanded its workforce to 546 employees. During the year, its solar assets generated approximately 250 million kWh of renewable electricity, while Greenet supplied approximately 420 million kWh of green electricity to corporate customers. J&V Energy further expanded its renewable generation capacity in 2026 by acquiring 42 operating solar plants totaling 187 MW. The portfolio is expected to generate approximately 270 million kWh annually, bringing the Group's overall annual solar generation potential to approximately 520 million kWh. Through its community solar programs, J&V Energy has also donated 32 kW across seven counties, reduced 18.6 tonnes of carbon emissions, and recorded 44,018 participant engagements through green-energy education. These achievements reflect J&V Energy's continued efforts to scale integrated low-carbon solutions while creating lasting environmental and community value. About Enterprise Asia Enterprise Asia is a non-governmental organization in pursuit of creating an Asia that is rich in entrepreneurship as an engine toward sustainable and progressive economic and social development within a world of economic equality. Its two pillars of existence are investment in people and responsible entrepreneurship. Enterprise Asia works with governments, NGOs, and other organizations to promote competitiveness and entrepreneurial development, uplifting the economic status of people across Asia and ensuring a legacy of hope, innovation, and courage for future generations. Please visit https://www.enterpriseasia.org/ for more information. About Asia Pacific Enterprise Awards Launched in 2007, the Asia Pacific Enterprise Awards is the region's most prestigious award for outstanding entrepreneurship, continuous innovation, and sustainable leadership. The Award provides a platform for companies and governments to recognize entrepreneurial excellence, hence spurring greater innovation, fair business practices, and growth in entrepreneurship. As a regional award, it groups together leading entrepreneurs as a powerful voice for entrepreneurship and serves as a by-invitation-only networking powerhouse. The program has grown to encompass 16 countries/ regions and markets all over Asia. For further information, please visit www.apea.asia.

ph.title: J&V Energy Accelerates Low-Carbon Growth with Integrated Energy and Infrastructure Solutions
ph.description: TAIPEI, Oct. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- J&V Energy Technology Co., Ltd. was recognized with the Corporate Excellence Award at the Asia Pacific Enterprise Awards (APEA) 2026 Taiwan Chapter, organized by Enterprise Asia, honoring its sustained growth and expanding contribution to the low-carbon energy transition. Established in 2016 and headquartered in Taipei, the company has evolved from a solar energy developer into a diversified energy and infrastructure group spanning renewable energy, green electricity trading, battery energy storage, water treatment, circular economy solutions, and AI infrastructure. J&V Energy's growth has been driven by its ability to combine technology, capital, and strategic partnerships across the energy value chain. The Group developed Taiwan's largest fishery-solar project at 128 MW, established Greenet as Taiwan's leading private green electricity trading platform, and developed Recharge Power into one of Taiwan's largest energy storage integrators. Recharge Power's cumulative deployments have reached 412 MW/1,055 MWh, including experience delivering Taiwan's largest single energy storage project. The Group's expanding operations now extend across Taiwan region, Japan, Australia, the Philippines, and other Asian markets. In 2025, the Group achieved 96.9% year-on-year growth in consolidated revenue and expanded its workforce to 546 employees. During the year, its solar assets generated approximately 250 million kWh of renewable electricity, while Greenet supplied approximately 420 million kWh of green electricity to corporate customers. J&V Energy further expanded its renewable generation capacity in 2026 by acquiring 42 operating solar plants totaling 187 MW. The portfolio is expected to generate approximately 270 million kWh annually, bringing the Group's overall annual solar generation potential to approximately 520 million kWh. Through its community solar programs, J&V Energy has also donated 32 kW across seven counties, reduced 18.6 tonnes of carbon emissions, and recorded 44,018 participant engagements through green-energy education. These achievements reflect J&V Energy's continued efforts to scale integrated low-carbon solutions while creating lasting environmental and community value. The meeting was attended by assistant commissioners from Shikarpur, Garhi Yasin, Khanpur and Lakhi talukas, along with representatives of the police, District Health Office, District Education Department (Primary and Secondary), National Programme, People’s Primary Healthcare Initiative (PPHI), District Intelligence Branch (DIB), district police focal persons, Union Council Medical Officers (UCMOs) and other relevant officials, said a press release. He informed the meeting that Shikarpur district comprises four talukas and 69 union councils. A target of administering polio vaccine drops to more than 310,414 children under the age of five has been set for the campaign. According to the briefing, 62 Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI) centres, 120 EPI vaccinators, 69 Union Council Medical Officers (UCMOs) and 923 mobile vaccination teams will participate in the campaign. In addition, staff from 14 union council partner organisations will assist in monitoring and operational activities to ensure the smooth conduct of the drive. ae.title: J&V Energy Accelerates Low-Carbon Growth with Integrated Energy and Infrastructure Solutions
ae.description: TAIPEI, Oct. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- J&V Energy Technology Co., Ltd. was recognized with the Corporate Excellence Award at the Asia Pacific Enterprise Awards (APEA) 2026 Taiwan Chapter, organized by Enterprise Asia, honoring its sustained growth and expanding contribution to the low-carbon energy transition. Established in 2016 and headquartered in Taipei, the company has evolved from a solar energy developer into a diversified energy and infrastructure group spanning renewable energy, green electricity trading, battery energy storage, water treatment, circular economy solutions, and AI infrastructure. J&V Energy's growth has been driven by its ability to combine technology, capital, and strategic partnerships across the energy value chain. The Group developed Taiwan's largest fishery-solar project at 128 MW, established Greenet as Taiwan's leading private green electricity trading platform, and developed Recharge Power into one of Taiwan's largest energy storage integrators. Recharge Power's cumulative deployments have reached 412 MW/1,055 MWh, including experience delivering Taiwan's largest single energy storage project. The Group's expanding operations now extend across Taiwan region, Japan, Australia, the Philippines, and other Asian markets. In 2025, the Group achieved 96.9% year-on-year growth in consolidated revenue and expanded its workforce to 546 employees. During the year, its solar assets generated approximately 250 million kWh of renewable electricity, while Greenet supplied approximately 420 million kWh of green electricity to corporate customers. J&V Energy further expanded its renewable generation capacity in 2026 by acquiring 42 operating solar plants totaling 187 MW. The portfolio is expected to generate approximately 270 million kWh annually, bringing the Group's overall annual solar generation potential to approximately 520 million kWh. Through its community solar programs, J&V Energy has also donated 32 kW across seven counties, reduced 18.6 tonnes of carbon emissions, and recorded 44,018 participant engagements through green-energy education. These achievements reflect J&V Energy's continued efforts to scale integrated low-carbon solutions while creating lasting environmental and community value. About Enterprise Asia Enterprise Asia is a non-governmental organization in pursuit of creating an Asia that is rich in entrepreneurship as an engine toward sustainable and progressive economic and social development within a world of economic equality. Its two pillars of existence are investment in people and responsible entrepreneurship. Enterprise Asia works with governments, NGOs, and other organizations to promote competitiveness and entrepreneurial development, uplifting the economic status of people across Asia and ensuring a legacy of hope, innovation, and courage for future generations. Please visit https://www.enterpriseasia.org/ for more information. About Asia Pacific Enterprise Awards Launched in 2007, the Asia Pacific Enterprise Awards is the region's most prestigious award for outstanding entrepreneurship, continuous innovation, and sustainable leadership. The Award provides a platform for companies and governments to recognize entrepreneurial excellence, hence spurring greater innovation, fair business practices, and growth in entrepreneurship. As a regional award, it groups together leading entrepreneurs as a powerful voice for entrepreneurship and serves as a by-invitation-only networking powerhouse. The program has grown to encompass 16 countries/ regions and markets all over Asia. For further information, please visit www.apea.asia.

ae.title: 16-Year Sleep Ends: 100 Satoshi-Era BTC Worth $8.3 Million Moves on a $1.22 Fee
ae.description: A dormant Bitcoin stash worth $8.3 million changed hands this week, and its owner paid just $1.22 for the transfer. The 100.02 BTC batch, mined in July 2010 during what's widely called the Satoshi-era, moved on Wednesday after sitting untouched for 16 years. The fee amounted to 1,467 satoshis, with a satoshi equaling one hundred-millionth of a bitcoin. At a price of roughly $83,000 per coin, the holdings carried a value near $8.3 million as they departed. Judging by Bitbo's highest registered BTC price for 2010, those same coins were worth only around $29 when they were first mined. Two mining rewards, one long sleep Bitcoin's network confirmed the transfer at 18:52 UTC in block 970,379 — one of the batches of transactions the network etches onto its public ledger roughly every 10 minutes. The funds were divided between two new addresses, each address functioning like an account number made of characters: one received 10 BTC, the other took in 90.02 BTC. Both destinations use the modern bc1q address format, which simply did not exist back when these coins were mined. Nothing within the transaction reveals who controls the funds, and relocating coins between addresses is not the same as cashing out. The stash itself began life as two separate mining payouts before becoming one. The larger piece, 50.02 BTC, arrived via block 70,522 on July 26, 2010, while the other 50 BTC came from block 70,748 two days later on July 28. A single transaction on July 30, 2010 folded the two together into the address that just released them. Back when 10,000 BTC bought two pizzas Nobody realized it at the time, but 2010 would go on to be a memorable year for Bitcoin. Laszlo Hanyecz, a programmer living in Florida, famously handed over 10,000 BTC for two pizzas — a tab of roughly $41. Since then, this week's stash has appreciated by more than a millionfold. The block reward has since been halved four separate times, most recently falling to 3.125 BTC with the April 2024 halving — a scheduled adjustment that arrives roughly every four years. A block mined today yields one-sixteenth of what those two 2010 blocks paid out. The address has seen action before That address hasn't exactly been idle over the years. It pushed out 100 BTC twice on August 8, 2015, another 100 BTC in December 2017, and 249 BTC in March 2018 — though those were different coins. Bitcoin accounts for money as individual chunks, somewhat like banknotes, so an address can spend part of its balance while the remainder sits untouched. Galaxy monitors the coins themselves rather than addresses, and noted that these specific coins had stayed put since 2010. "We maintain a complete ledger of every single UTXO and all their historical movements (about 1.7 terabytes). This address has been somewhat active in the past, but these specific coins have not moved since 2010. We track the coins." Galaxy Research wrote that in a post published October 8, 2026. Old coins from Bitcoin's early days keep stirring Coins mined during Bitcoin's first years are known as Satoshi-era, a nod to the network's pseudonymous founder, Satoshi Nakamoto, and they have been surfacing in clusters. In February 2025, a 50 BTC batch that had been valued at $0.10 per coin when mined sprang back to life after roughly 15 years, by which point it was worth about $5 million. That holder skipped a test transaction — the small trial payment people typically send first to confirm the destination works. In August, 49.97 BTC first received in July 2011, back when Bitcoin traded below $15, woke up after about 15 years and traveled on to a wallet that Arkham, a blockchain analytics platform, has tagged as FalconX, a prime broker catering to trading firms. A label by itself doesn't prove a sale occurred. And between August 16 and 26, six wallets that had been dormant since 2011, 2012 or 2014 shifted 553.59 BTC — approximately $40 million. Two of those wallets carried tags linked to a New York lawsuit asking a court to declare 39,069 dormant addresses abandoned property. As of Thursday, both the 10 BTC and the 90.02 BTC were still resting in their new addresses, with no onward transfers recorded. So Bitcoin holders, take a breath: this whale isn't offloading coins — at least not yet.

Re: Clinical update: Assessment and management of Helicobacter pylori infection and who should be tested
za.description: Agreement: I Agree Body: Dear Editor The issue of who should be tested for H. pylori was addressed by Public Health England in a publication which stated that "patients with unexplained iron deficiency anaemia, after negative endoscopic investigation has excluded gastric and colonic malignancy, and investigations have been carried out for other causes, including cancer, idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura, vitamin B12 deficiency" should come under the heading of patients who should be tested for H. pylori[1]. In principle, those recommendations should apply even when a patient presents with unusual manifestations of iron deficiency anaemia such as koilonychia[2], or Plummer-Vinson syndrome[3],[4],5],[6]. Hence the rationale for H. pylori testing in a patient with Plummer-Vinson syndrome in whom duodenal biopsy was non diagnostic for coeliac disease, and in whom colonoscopy had also been non diagnostic for colon cancer [7]. H. pylori gastritis is also a risk factor for vitamin B12 deficiency[8] and, hence, subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord[9]. Accordingly, the workup of patients with vitamin B12 deficiency, including patients with myeloneuropathy attributable to nitrous oxide abuse[10] should include tests for H. pylori[10]. dz.title: مستشفى بن زرجب ينظم الأيام الدولية للطب الداخلي: مناقشة مستجدات التكفل بالامراض المزمنة والنادرة
dz.description: وهران: انطلقت اليوم فعاليات الأيام الدولية الرابعة للطب الداخلي،المنظم من طرف المركز الاستشفائي الجامعي الدكتور بن زرجب بمشاركة نحو 350 طبيبًا، من أطباء عامين وأخصائيين، إلى جانب خبراء من داخل الوطن وخارجه، في تظاهرة علمية تهدف إلى تعزيز التكوين الطبي المستمر وتبادل الخبرات حول مستجدات التشخيص والعلاج، لاسيما في مجال الأمراض المزمنة والنادرة. وأكد الدكتور شامي محمد الأمين، المختص في الطب الداخلي ورئيس المؤتمر، أن هذه الأيام العلمية ترمي إلى تعزيز التحسيس وتبادل التجارب والخبرات بين الممارسين الصحيين، من خلال برنامج علمي يتناول أربعة محاور أساسية، يتعلق المحور الأول بداء السكري، باعتباره من الأمراض التي تتطلب متابعة طبية مستمرة وتكفلًا ملائمًا، فيما يخصص المحور الثاني لموضوع تخثر الدم، إلى جانب محور ثالث يتناول الأمراض الرئوية وعلاقتها بالطب الداخلي، بينما يسلط المحور الرابع الضوء على الأمراض النادرة، بهدف تبسيط المعارف المرتبطة بها ومساعدة الأطباء العامين على تحسين التكفل بالمصابين بها. وأوضح المتحدث أن المؤتمر يشهد مشاركة أطباء قدموا من مختلف ولايات الوطن، على غرار الجزائر العاصمة وقسنطينة وبجاية وتيزي وزو، إلى جانب مشاركة خبراء من الخارج، ما يتيح فرصة لتبادل المعارف والاطلاع على التجارب العلمية والطبية الحديثة في التخصص. من جهتها، أكدت الدكتورة منيرة سميتي، المشاركة من تونس، أهمية هذه اللقاءات العلمية في تعزيز التعاون بين الأطباء وتبادل الخبرات في المجالات الطبية المتخصصة، مشيرة إلى أنها قدمت محاضرة حول إصابات الرئتين لدى مرضى التهاب الأوعية الدموية، تناولت خلالها المستجدات الطبية والتطورات العلمية المتعلقة بعلاج هذه الحالات. وأضافت المتحدثة أنها ليست المرة الأولى التي تشارك فيها في مؤتمر علمي بالجزائر، معربة عن سعادتها بحضور هذه التظاهرة، التي تشكل، حسبها، فرصة لتقاسم التجارب والمعارف مع الزملاء الجزائريين، بما يسهم في تطوير الممارسات الطبية وتحسين جودة التكفل بالمرضى. وفي السياق ذاته، شدد الدكتور خالد السعيد، أحد المشاركين في المؤتمر، على أهمية مناقشة الأمراض المزمنة والاضطرابات المرتبطة بالأوعية الدموية، إلى جانب الأمراض النادرة التي لا تزال تطرح تحديات أمام المنظومة الصحية، خاصة ما تعلق بالتشخيص المبكر وتوفير العلاج المناسب. وأشار المتحدث إلى أن المصابين بالأمراض النادرة يواجهون في بعض الحالات صعوبات في الحصول على العلاج والتكفل الملائم، الأمر الذي يستدعي تعزيز الاهتمام بهذه الفئة وتحسين ظروف رعايتها الصحية، مثمنًا في هذا الإطار التعليمات الرئيس الجمهورية تبون عبد المجيد إالتى دعما الى تًوفير ضمان التكفل الأمثل بمرضى الأمراض النادرة.

mg.title: EXÉCUTION BUDGÉTAIRE - Le Premier ministre tape du poing sur la table
mg.description: Mamitiana Rajaonarison hausse le ton face à la lenteur de l’exécution budgétaire. Il exige l’identification immédiate des blocages et des solutions pour atteindre 100 % des objectifs en 2026. Une remontrance. C’est ce que Mamitiana Rajaonarison, Premier ministre, a adressé aux acteurs de la gestion des finances publiques et de l’exécution des investissements publics, à Anosy, mercredi. Des remontrances motivées par le constat du taux d’exécution budgétaire faible pour cet exercice 2026. Face aux responsables de la chaîne budgétaire, le locataire de Mahazoarivo a fixé une trajectoire sans équivoque, « identifier les obstacles qui ralentissent les dépenses publiques et trouver sans délai les moyens de les lever ». L’objectif immédiat est tout autant sans ambages, « arriver à un taux d’exécution budgétaire de 100 % pour cette année 2026 ». Des instructions qui enclenchent une course contre la montre étant donné que le ministère de l’Économie et des Finances a déjà fixé la fin des engagements budgétaires le 2 novembre. Le constat durant la réunion de mercredi est qu’à l’entame du dernier trimestre de l’année, le taux d’exécution budgétaire est de 44,2 %. Une contre-performance qui pénalise surtout les investissements publics, particulièrement pour les projets financés par les fonds extérieurs. S’agissant de ces derniers, le taux d’exécution est de 20,3 % selon le ministère de l’Économie et des Finances. Pour les projets d’investissement financés par l’État, la situation est relativement meilleure, avec 63,7 % de taux d’exécution. Faute de décaissement, une somme de plus de « 1 000 milliards d’ariary », selon Mamitiana Rajaonarison, est bloquée à la Banque centrale. « La Banque centrale nous a dit qu’il s’agit d’une première », ajoute-t-il. Bien que le montant soit retentissant, une faible exécution des budgets d’investissement témoigne d’une faible performance étatique dans ce domaine. Un exemple avancé par le docteur Herinjatovo Ramiarison, ministre de l’Économie et des Finances : le retard dans l’exécution d’un projet routier représente un manque à gagner de 2 % du Produit intérieur brut (PIB), soit 360 millions de dollars. Expéditivité « Nous savons quand commence et quand se termine la période d’exécution budgétaire, alors pourquoi toujours attendre la dernière minute pour s’y mettre ? », déplore le chef du gouvernement, en faisant part d’un certain agacement. Un sentiment qui, à l’entendre, découle des demandes de dérogation enregistrées à la primature par des entités publiques, lorsque le ministère de l’Économie leur a transmis une circulaire leur rappelant le deadline du 2 novembre. Par ailleurs, il ne s’agit pas juste d’accélérer les démarches d’engagement et de décaissement des crédits, mais surtout de faire qu’ils aient un impact positif sur le quotidien de la population. La réunion d’Anosy s’est donc évertuée à identifier les blocages et à trouver les solutions pour les lever. Le Premier ministre martèle le fait que le but est d’agir « immédiatement » pour lever les goulots d’étranglement. Sur le plateau de la télévision publique TVM, dimanche, il a utilisé le terme « expéditivité ». Une expression fréquemment mise en avant par le locataire de Mahazoarivo est également que « si le blocage est une personne, on le remplace, si c’est une question de procédure, de règle ou de loi, nous allons le modifier». Des mots qu’il a réaffirmés à Anosy, mercredi. Le problème concernant le taux d’exécution budgétaire n’est toutefois pas nouveau. Les bailleurs internationaux, notamment la Banque mondiale, ont déjà tiré la sonnette d’alarme quant à la faiblesse du taux de décaissement des financements extérieurs en raison de la lourdeur budgétaire. S’agissant des financements extérieurs, le Premier ministre Rajaonarison soutient cependant que la lourdeur des procédures se retrouve aussi du côté des partenaires internationaux. Il concède que cette situation résulte du manque de confiance envers l’État. Le chef du gouvernement reconnaît ainsi qu’il revient à Madagascar de faire preuve de bonne gouvernance afin de rassurer ses partenaires et ainsi alléger les différentes étapes de validation techniques et financières. Lors de la séance d’adoption de la loi de finances rectificative, à l’Assemblée nationale, en juin, les députés, eux aussi, ont pointé du doigt le faible taux d’exécution budgétaire. Une situation criante dans des secteurs sensibles comme l’énergie, l’eau ou l’éducation. Devant les membres de la Chambre basse, Mamitiana Rajaonarison s’est déjà engagé à « briser » les causes de la lourdeur administrative. Une task force cogite sur le sujet justement. En attendant que les mesures nécessaires soient prises, les procédures toujours en vigueur risquent de transformer l’objectif d’atteindre un taux d’exécution budgétaire de 100 % d’ici le 2 novembre en une mission impossible. Garry Fabrice Ranaivoson
